definitions.explanation: Electromagnetic radiation used for communication, broadcasting, and other technological applications.
In casual usage, refers to the quality of wireless signal reception.

examples.japanese: {電波|でんぱ}{時計|どけい}は{正確|せいかく}だ。
examples.notes: {電波|でんぱ}{時計|どけい} = radio-controlled clock

examples.japanese: {電波|でんぱ}で{情報|じょうほう}を{送信|そうしん}する。
examples.english: Information is transmitted via radio waves.

examples.japanese: テレビの{電波|でんぱ}を{受信|じゅしん}するためにアンテナが{必要|ひつよう}だ。
examples.english: An antenna is needed to receive TV radio waves.

examples.japanese: {携帯|けいたい}{電話|でんわ}の{電波|でんぱ}が{人体|じんたい}に{与|あた}える{影響|えいきょう}について{研究|けんきゅう}が{進|すす}んでいる。
examples.english: Research is progressing on the effects of cell phone radio waves on the human body.

examples.japanese: ここは{電波|でんぱ}が{悪|わる}い。
{山|やま}の{中|なか}で{電波|でんぱ}が{入|はい}らない。
examples.english: There's no signal in the mountains.

examples.japanese: {電波|でんぱ}が{弱|よわ}くて{動画|どうが}が{見|み}られない。
examples.english: The signal is weak and I can't watch videos.

examples.japanese: {地下|ちか}に{入|はい}ると{電波|でんぱ}が{届|とど}かなくなることがある。
examples.english: When you go underground, the signal sometimes doesn't reach.

examples.japanese: {新|あたら}しい{基地局|きちきょく}ができてから、この{辺|あた}りは{電波|でんぱ}がよくなった。
examples.english: Since the new base station was built, the signal in this area has improved.

notes:
TECHNICAL USE:
- {電波|でんぱ}を{発信|はっしん}する (to transmit radio waves)
- {電波|でんぱ}を{受信|じゅしん}する (to receive radio waves)
- {電波|でんぱ}{障害|しょうがい} (radio interference)
- {電波|でんぱ}{法|ほう} (Radio Law)

EVERYDAY USE:
- {電波|でんぱ}が{悪|わる}い (poor signal/reception)
- {電波|でんぱ}が{入|はい}らない (no signal)
- {電波|でんぱ}{時計|どけい} (radio-controlled clock)

SLANG (dated): {電波|でんぱ}{系|けい} was used to describe someone who seems disconnected from reality or has strange ideas (not recommended to use).

SCIENCE: {電波|でんぱ} is part of the electromagnetic spectrum, with frequencies lower than infrared.
